item.title: Blood, Mice, and Tears: A Mouse Guard Retrospective
item.description:
“It matters not who you fight for, but what you fight for.”

So says the inscription of Lockhaven Walls.

Among the Mice Territories, the Guard stands ready to protect: the smallest creatures with the bravest hearts. Lockhaven, their walled home of muroidian proportions, is nestled deep in stone, carved like the walls of Minas Tirith. The mice arm themselves with sword and spear, bow and blade, and fight to protect those who cannot protect themselves from any manner of beast. The weasels, now driven out of the Mice Territories; the wolves that haunt the edge of the Scent Border; snakes that live in underground nests; crabs with vicious appetites. Truly, for a mouse, all things are dangerous.

item.title: Project Hail Mary and A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms
item.description: Project Hail Mary looked great. It sounded great. Everyone in the film was acting. But the story? The story was a bit lackluster, at least for this author. I’d been hearing so many amazing things about the film; people were raving about it online and people at work were telling me I just had to see it, especially since I’m a known reader and a known science fiction enjoyer.

item.title: What is Military Science Fiction Good For, Anyways?
item.description: Military science fiction, like all things, can be multiple things at once. It can be dystopia, thriller, or horror. It can be a promotion of the military and all the accolades and kinship that come with it: at the same time it can be a cutting critique of the very same kinds of ideals and the humanity that one must set aside to follow orders.

item.title: (It's All) Pulp Fiction
item.description:
It’s come to my attention that I’m a pulp reader. Perhaps I always was.

When I was younger I consumed primarily sci-fi and fantasy, and while that’s still true, my new love has evolved into a regression, at least temporally: pulp fiction. The term, as many know, comes from the kind of paper on which these stories were printed on—a kind of cheap, acidic paper that deteriorates and yellows over time. It was first used to refer to “pulp magazines” which were popular from the late 1890’s through 1950’s.

item.title: A Glossary of Terms
item.description:
Welcome to the Captain’s Blog Glossary of Terms. Until the Captain gets off her ass and actually modifies this page to be a proper glossary, you can use Ctrl + F in order to search for terms. Terms are organized alphbetically and will be added on an as-needed basis. Apologies for the inconvinience.

Erotica: A sub-genre of the Romance Genre. These works are primarily concerned with telling stories of an erotic or pornographic nature, however, the emphasis on the story itself may be just as important as the soft-core (or sometimes hard-core) porn.

item.title: A Word From the Author
item.description:
Captain’s Blog, stardate -296463.3042237442.
Today is the day that I begin posting to the Captain’s Blog. It will surely be an endeavor to maintain a consistent schedule throughout the busy ups-and-downs of life aboard the WWW-Internet, however, I am confident that I am locquacious enough to keep good company and a font of ideas flowing.

Though my work may be, at times, quite lengthy, they are not works of academic quality, nor should be considered as such. They are merely the opinions of a young captain navigating the starry seas of the post-modern pop-media landscape.
